newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Cemig shares drop on scrapped auction.
newsitem.headline: Cemig shares drop on scrapped auction.

text.p: Shares of Cemig dropped on Sao Paulo's stock exchange after Minas Gerais state scrapped plans to sell a 33-percent stake in the state power firm, brokers said.
Cemig's voting common were down 13.7 percent at 39.70 reais while its preferred was off 2.02 percent at 34.00 reais at 1610 local/1310 EST on the Sao Paulo bolsa.
Despite Cemig's fall, the wider market was up a slight 0.23 percent at 69,283 points on weak trade of about 173 million reais ($167 million).

The auction of Cemig common, or ordinary, shares was slated for January's first half but was suspended after federal officials decided not to extend a repayment deadline on a debt owed by the state, a company official said.

The federal development bank BNDES insisted the first tranche of a 430 million-real loan to Minas Gerais state be repaid as scheduled. The loan was backed by debentures convertible to the 33-percent of Cemig common that the state had hoped to sell to a strategic foreign investor.
While volume was weak through most of the day, Telebras and other leading shares picked up some toward the late afternoon.
Bolsa benchmark Telebras preferred was up 0.24 percent at 79.19 reais while its common was up 0.41 percent at 73.30 reais.
Meanwhile, state oil firm Petrobras's preferred was up 1.23 percent while state power holding Eletrobras rose 1.22 percent.
